Shek Mun AVoIP Operations Report — Wednesday 11 November 2026

Full-day evidence from eight two-hourly read-only log captures (08:00–22:00 HKT) across Rooms SM-11-01 to SM-11-08, the evening switch cross-check (15/16 logins), and a comparison against Tuesday 10 November. No device was reset, reconfigured or restarted by this monitoring.

Day verdict: a day that recovered completely by evening — all eight rooms online at the 20:00 capture — on a continuing source-side pattern (the longest stop, SM-11-05 at ~4 h 32 m, covered almost a whole class in an empty room), before a day-end shutdown wave left seven rooms dark after their classes and only SM-11-08 online; the one infrastructure case is SM-11-06's lectern segment, unreachable at day end with its decoder looping for want of an encoder — first follow-up tomorrow morning.

Observations — day analysis

Two stories today: source-side behaviour all day, and one genuine infrastructure outage at day end. Apart from SM-11-06, every sustained loss began with a lectern-PC source stopping and the decoders following; the switch cross-check is negative for every one of them. SM-11-06 is different in kind — a whole device group (the lectern switch itself included) unreachable while the rack side stays up — and it is tracked separately, as a segment problem, not as another source stop.

Teaching impact, honestly weighed. The long stops that truly covered classes: SM-11-05's near-whole SS6102-L01 (room empty — booked but unattended, recorded as an observation; the verdicts followed the booking), the first ~13 minutes of SM-11-06's only evening class, SM-11-03's afternoon tail, and the day-end wave's tails (~58 / 10 / 6 / 3 minutes in four rooms). Against that, the afternoon stops all recovered before their evening classes (11, 9 and 4 minutes ahead for SM-11-01, 04 and 03), and the 20:00 capture found all eight rooms online.

The evening recovery wave deserves its line. Five rooms' stops ended inside 18:27–18:56, tight against their 18:30 / 19:00 class starts — the mirror image of the morning's pre-class recoveries. Recorded as timing only, no causation claimed; it is the same shape as sources being woken for class.

Yesterday's signature did not repeat as a cluster. The roughly-one-hour stop interval (five rooms within eight morning minutes yesterday, twice more at midday) appears nowhere as a group today; stop times are spread across the day and sit against class ends, lunch gaps and the evening close. The lectern-PC settings check stays on the suggestion list on the strength of the accumulated source-side evidence, not of a repeated cluster.

Two discovery loops, two different causes — not to be conflated. SM-11-08's power-on loop self-stopped with a matching switch link flap, as yesterday. SM-11-06's day-end loop is the direct consequence of an unreachable encoder path at the baseline rate (~13 lines/s); its remedy is segment connectivity, not the channel-assignment fix that cured SM-11-03 in October.

USB storms: quiet day, four at night — again. After the morning power-on cluster the decoder side was clean all day (one 17-line burst at 18:35 excepted); at night all four known flappers stormed together for the second consecutive evening. SM-11-08 TV-DEC-2 proved again that a storm and a live picture coexist; the other three storms sit alongside their rooms' shutdown-wave losses.

Evidence conflicts were named, not smoothed. The 14:00 run's automatic still-down flags for SM-11-01 were overturned by PTZ plus thumbnails; the 16:00 run judged SM-11-03 from evidence an hour before its buffer could show the loss; tonight SM-11-06's picture-sized thumbnails (lock-screen clock 10:08) lost to PTZ, log and three failed probes. Each case is written up where it happened.

Suggestions (advice only — nothing was executed)

  1. SM-11-06 lectern segment — on-site check before tomorrow's first class (new, first). At 21:55 the snapshot listed SW-Lectern (172.18.22.26), both AVoIP encoders, PCU-Lectern, AVProc-Pi5, Dock-2ch and USB-PC as fail while every rack-side device was ok; the satellite switch login failed and TV-DEC-1 is looping for want of its encoder. Check the lectern switch's power first (PCU-Lectern itself is on the fail list — lectern power may be interrupted), then its uplink, then the two encoders. Once the segment is back the decoder loop should stop on its own; verify with one capture run. The outage start is bracketed 20:15–21:55; no single device is called faulty before the segment is restored.
  2. Lectern PC sleep / power-saving settings — check all rooms, SM-11-05, SM-11-01 and SM-11-03 first (restated, evidence updated). Every sustained loss today other than SM-11-06 was source-side: SM-11-05 stopped for ~4 h 32 m across almost a whole class, SM-11-01 for ~4 h 11 m in the afternoon, SM-11-03 for ~2 h 53 m, and the day-end wave covered the last ~58 minutes of SM-11-05's evening class. Verify each lectern PC's sleep / display-off / scheduled-shutdown settings (nothing should trigger mid-class), with the source-side list in the same visit: PC power/BIOS timing, Duplicate display mode, HDMI into the encoder, encoder PoE.
  3. USB path field checks for all four flapping decoders — one combined list (restated). SM-11-01 TV-DEC-1, SM-11-02 TV-DEC-1, SM-11-07 TV-DEC-1 and SM-11-08 TV-DEC-2 stormed together for a second consecutive evening (1,334 lines in tonight's window, all still running at capture end), after a morning power-on cluster. Check each unit's USB cable / hub path / TV USB port. The Saturday field-check list has had no results reported; nothing is assumed done.
  4. SM-11-05's in-class stops — ask the day's users (new, light). This room stopped twice inside booked classes today (10:28–15:01 across almost the whole class, and from 21:01 covering the last ~58 minutes), with PTZ showing the room empty/dark both times. If practical, establish how those classes actually ran (ended early, or taught another way) so future same-shaped cases can separate 'booked but unattended' from genuinely affected teaching. Enquiry only — no action on any device.
  5. SM-11-01 TV-DEC-2 temperature at 48 °C — watch (new, light). The day's highest target temperature, at the top of the 45–48 °C watch band, status ok and no thermal lines in any log. Worth a glance in tomorrow's patrols; only if it sits at or above 49 °C does it become a heat follow-up. Nothing is done here.
  6. Switch logging levels for R4–R7 (level 5) — for Danny to consider (restated). Today's one correlated case sat on SM-11-08's level-6 satellite; IGMP-grade material for the other four rooms still needs level 6 to be conclusive. A configuration change — not executed here. SM-11-06's satellite follows item 1, not this one.

Method & sources

Read-only throughout: P3000 #LOG-ACTION? + #LOG-TAIL? 1000 per unit via the Tailscale tunnel (30 targets: PC/Laptop encoders and TV decoders, Rooms SM-11-01..08; Common Area, Mac and Dante encoders and audio decoders excluded), AV Monitoring snapshot.json, Kramer Manager thumbnails via the arm-and-retry route, PTZ snapshots, and the Netgear AV-UI switch fetch (buffered log, logging level, port statistics, multicast groups) for all 16 room switches (SM-11-06's satellite login failed and was recorded and skipped, never retried). Loss state is judged per decoder from event order in its synced buffer; the automatic pass's known biases (flagging same-second re-locks as still-down, storm-rolled signal lines, stale thumbnail caches) were corrected case by case against the raw logs and evidence, with conflicts stated. Full per-run analyses and the day consolidation: hidden_files/avoip-log-capture/2026-11-11-*/ANALYSIS.md and 2026-11-11-2200/DAILY-SUMMARY.md; raw switch JSON in 2026-11-11-switch/. This report's figures come only from those verified files.
